subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: How should OpenClaw handle legacy Telegram outbound delivery-queue rows that have ambiguous network-send evidence but no `recoveryState` marker?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose between preserving possibly-unsent legacy replies and avoiding user-visible duplicate Telegram sends without maintainer intent for this upgrade edge case.

options.title: Quarantine ambiguous legacy Telegram rows
options.body: Classify matching legacy rows as unsafe to replay, move or fail them with an operator-visible diagnostic, and add restart-replay regression coverage.

options.title: Keep them pending until reconciliation exists
options.body: Avoid duplicate sends by refusing replay while preserving the row for a future Telegram reconciliation capability or manual operator action.

options.title: Continue replaying unmarked rows
options.body: Maximize delivery of possibly unsent legacy messages but accept that some users may receive duplicate Telegram replies and mirrored transcript entries.

recommendation.title: Quarantine ambiguous legacy Telegram rows
recommendation.body: Classify matching legacy rows as unsafe to replay, move or fail them with an operator-visible diagnostic, and add restart-replay regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the most recent merged recovery hardening in the same queue lifecycle and are best positioned to judge the remaining upgrade-policy fit.
